families.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Gyro)
families.about: Gyro-S (27.6 GB of memory) and Gyro-M (35 GB): the smallest sizes, for PCs with little memory; 58 and 92 GB downloads (the files include the n-gram table)

sizes.about: the smallest option, for PCs with little memory (27.6 GB of VRAM + RAM together); lower quality than the 2-3-bit sizes, and the 2-bit Q2_0 decodes faster
about IQ3_XXS quality with about 20% less GPU memory (35 GB of VRAM + RAM together); decodes about 16-21% slower than Q2_0 on 12 GB cards

families.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (NVFP4)
families.about: 4-bit NVFP4 experts, NVIDIA cards; a 128 GB download, ~80 GB of RAM to keep every expert in RAM

sizes.about: best quality of the NVFP4 versions (GPTQ, sergqwer's strata-nvfp4 pack); RTX 50 has FP4 tensor cores, other NVIDIA cards run it at 8-bit precision
NVIDIA's own NVFP4 checkpoint (plain rounding), converted by sergqwer; the same size and speed as NVFP4

NVIDIA's FP4, trained for FP4 (NVIDIA's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local) - slightly faster on short prompts; a 102 GB download that this PC turns into a Strata pack once (about 20-40 minutes, 110 GB more disk); RTX 50 cards have FP4 tensor cores, other NVIDIA cards run it at 8-bit precision. It reads pictures (the shared Qwen3.8-Flash-Next encoder)

families.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
families.about: a big model that runs on a PC with a 12 GB card and 64 GB of RAM (the two official 2-bit versions: 257 or 274 GB of disk, about 5-7 tokens a second) or, in Unsloth's 508 GB version, on several graphics cards

sizes.about: the smaller official version: 138 GB of model + 111 GB n-gram table + 8 GB drafter (257 GB of disk). Runs on a PC with a 12 GB card and 40-64 GB of RAM at about 5-7 tokens a second; quality about 15.5% above the original model's perplexity (code and agent work 5-9%)
sizes.on_this_pc: tight: it needs about 263 GB of free disk space (the rest of the download and its preparation) and this computer has 38 GB free; free some space or choose another drive when you install it (slow here: this computer has 32 GB of RAM and the set was measured with 46-64 GB, so most of its experts are read from the SSD; it can still be installed (the smaller 1.75 bpw version suits this computer better))

lines: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, ISTA-DAS 2.00 bpw: a 257 GB download (138 GB of model, 111 GB n-gram table, 8 GB drafter). Quality: about 15.5% above the original model's perplexity (code and agent work about 5-9% above).

The n-gram table stays on the SSD and is read a few rows for each word: use an NVMe drive for the model files (a slow disk makes every word slower). The same table serves every ISTA-DAS set, so installing another one downloads it once.

Graphics memory: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti (16 GB). About 793 of the 15,360 experts (7 GB) stay on the card; the other 14,567 (125 GB) are computed on the CPU from RAM, and the ones RAM cannot hold are read from the SSD when a word needs them.

Measured on an RTX 5070 (12 GB) with 64 GB of RAM and a 3.6 GB/s NVMe drive: answers about 4.7 tokens a second, a 4,000-token prompt read at 121 tokens a second; an RTX 3060 (12 GB) with 46 GB of RAM: about 7.2 tokens a second; four Radeon AI PRO R9700 cards: about 31 tokens a second. Other computers are slower or faster by what their cards, RAM and drive can do.
warnings: This computer has 32 GB of RAM and this model was measured with 46 GB and 64 GB. With less, most experts come from the SSD while it answers: it works but is slow (a word can take seconds). More RAM fixes it. It is still allowed.

lines: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (UD-Q8_K_XL): a 508 GB download. In memory it needs 306 GB: 289 GB of experts (15,360 of 18.8 MB) and 17 GB of attention and other dense weights.

Its n-gram table (203 GB of the download) stays on the SSD and is read a few rows for each word it writes: it is not counted in RAM, but a slow disk (SATA, a network drive, a USB disk) makes every word slower. Use an NVMe drive for the model files.
One card (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, 16 GB): the dense weights (16 GB) and 22 of the 15,360 experts (0 GB) go in its memory, the other 15,338 experts (288 GB) are computed on the CPU from RAM.
The other 15,338 experts (288 GB) are computed on the CPU, read in place from the model's files: they need that much free RAM to stay cached (297 GB with 9 GB for the system and the engine).

Measured on 4 x Radeon AI PRO R9700 (32 GB) with 251 GB of RAM: prompts of 3,000 tokens read at 143-181 tokens a second, answers at 25-31 tokens a second (--tp 2); one answer at a time. Other computers are slower or faster by what their cards and RAM can hold; this engine has been run on AMD cards.
warnings: The dense weights need ~16 GB of graphics memory on the card and NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti (16 GB) has hardly that: the engine may stop at the start (out of graphics memory). More or bigger cards fix it; it is still allowed.

This computer has 32 GB of RAM and 297 GB would keep the CPU's share of the experts cached: about 266 GB of them are read from the SSD while the model answers, which is slow (a word can take seconds). More RAM or more graphics memory fixes it. It is still allowed.

fields.label: Thinking token budget
fields.hint: Leave blank for the model default.

fields.label: Fit output to remaining context
fields.hint: Shortens the requested output cap when the prompt leaves less room.

fields.label: Anthropic thinking
fields.hint: Follow the model default or think only when requested.

fields.label: API model aliases
fields.hint: Comma-separated names clients may use for this model.

fields.label: Draft layer (MTP)
fields.hint: The draft layer guesses several words ahead, which makes answers faster, and costs about 1 GB of graphics memory and some RAM. Turn it off if the model stops while it starts, or the card is small: the expert cache gets that memory back and answers are slower. Default is on.

fields.label: Drafting
fields.hint: Which drafter guesses words ahead to make answers faster, one at a time. Auto (recommended) is DFlash2 for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next where the engine has it, the MTP otherwise. DFlash2 downloads a 1.2 GB drafter once, the MTP its draft layer once. If DFlash2 cannot run (several requests at once), the MTP is used alone and Details says why. Off turns the drafter off.

fields.label: MTP per request
fields.hint: Each concurrent request uses the draft layer. Left alone, Strata turns it on for one graphics card with 24 GB or more and several requests at once, and off otherwise; choose on or off here to decide yourself.

fields.label: Speed (DeepSeek)
fields.hint: Faster uses 5 of 6 experts per word: a small quality change, usually not noticeable. Full quality uses all 6. Left alone, the engine picks Faster on a PC whose graphics cards total 16 GB or less.

fields.label: Concurrent requests
fields.hint: More slots need more memory and can slow each response.

fields.label: Layer split
fields.hint: auto, or increasing split points such as 18 or 16,32.

fields.label: Use one GPU when the model fits
KV cache K format
fields.hint: Leave Default to use the model KV format, or pick a native K cache quantization (--cache-type-k).

fields.label: KV cache V format
fields.hint: Leave Default to use the model KV format, or pick a native V cache quantization (--cache-type-v).

fields.label: Spin(8) KV rotation mode
fields.hint: Optional native Spin(8) KV cache transform (--spin8-mode).

fields.label: Spin(8) capsule JSON path
fields.hint: Optional verified Spin(8) native capsule JSON path (--spin8-native-config). Requires Spin(8) capsule SHA-256.

fields.label: Spin(8) capsule SHA-256
fields.hint: Expected 64-character lowercase SHA-256 digest of the Spin(8) capsule JSON (--spin8-native-sha256).
